utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. I would like to greet all the people present in the courtroom, the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, as well as all the people present in this courtroom. The Trial Chamber will hand down a few oral decisions pertaining to applications made by the Defence. I shall read it out slowly. Oral decision relating to a number of applications made by the Defence with a view to being granted extension of time. On the 18th of September, 2007, the Defence applied orally before the Chamber to consider as a priority the application filed on the 4th of September relating to abuse of process on the part of the Prosecution. The Defence has also applied for a suspension of response deadlines to the motions filed by the Prosecution referred to in its application of the 4th of September. The Prosecution did not object. The Trial Chamber has decided to consider the application of the 4th of September as a priority. However, it does not grant the oral application made by the Defence pertaining to a suspension of response time to the mentioned -- above-mentioned motions. The Trial Chamber recalls that it has already granted extension of time, substantial extension of time, when responses were to be made. Also, on the 18th of September, 2007, the Defence applied for an extension of time to respond to the Prosecution's motion of the 11th of September, 2007, applying for the admission of 28 exhibits. The Prosecution, however, did not object. The Trial Chamber notes on a preliminary basis that it seems that some of the documents referred to in the motion should be shown to the witnesses during the hearing. In light of the progress of the Prosecution's case, this motion will also be considered as a priority by the Trial Chamber. Consequently, the Trial Chamber cannot grant the application for extension of time and dismisses the motion. In addition, at yesterday's hearing the Defence applied for an extension of time to respond to the Prosecution's motion of the 10th of September, 2007, asking for the admission of written statements and transcripts pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence relating to the Heliodrom. The Prosecution did not object. The Trial Chamber grants an extension of two weeks until the 8th of October, 2007. Lastly, the Trial Chamber notes that on the 18th of September, 2007, the Prosecution filed a confidential motion asking for a particular witness to be heard by videolink. The Trial Chamber is asking the Defence to respond to this motion by next Monday at the latest, Monday the 24th of September, 2007. So much for the decisions which have been handed down. I will now ask the usher to drop the blinds, and I shall give the floor to the registrar so that we can have an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One of the parties have submitted list of objections to document tendered by the OTP through Witness E. The list of documents submitted by 5D shall be given Exhibit number IC 665. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Let's move back into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please raise the blinds.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're in open session. Mr. Scott, we have just completed the programme of the week. For next week we have a witness? There is no problem there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, Mr. President. That's correct. We have a witness. We have one witness who is scheduled for next week and it just depends on if we wind up taking the full week or not, but he is -- everything is arranged and he will be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me also indicate that the week of the 1st October, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of October we will be having our hearing in the afternoon, but there's another trial that has been cancelled for lack of witnesses, so it could occur that we have our hearing Monday afternoon and then the following days, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, in the morning, which would mean 9.00 to 12.30, followed by a break between 12.30 and 2.30, and then work from 2.30 to 5.00. This would give us a little bit more time during that week. I'm just letting you know. Mr. Scott, I know that the legal officer had drawn your attention to that possibility and you will have to plan for the witnesses accordingly. That's what I wanted to inform you of. We still have a few more minutes left. Does the Defence have any comments to make? Mr. Karnavas, who has been very quiet today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have. I just have one question and that's for next week. As I understand it, it's three days for this witness. That's what the Court has allowed, or am I to -- did I misunderstand, that it could be up to four days?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Let me answer immediately. The Prosecutor had planned for three days. Three days. And the fourth day we will not have a hearing, but as far as I'm concerned there will be a pre-trial -- a status hearing, and so I will be busy the fourth day given that the Prosecution had only planned for three days for that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just wanted some sort of [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I was not clear I apologise. I meant -- you're absolutely right. I mean that We expected the witness to be three days but unexpectedly if it went over we would have the fourth day but I don't expect that. I don't think anyone expects that to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions? In that case I'd like to thank you and we shall meet again on Monday at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.48 p.m.,
